notes: Use-case: payments customer-facing chat for fraud-ops + high-volume embeddings for transaction search.
Throughput target: 1,200 concurrent chat requests (avg request size ~220 tokens) across the fleet; peak 2.5k rps for embeddings jobs during batch runs.
Latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for streaming chat responses; 99th < 350ms is desired for critical flows.
Availability target: 99.95% across primary regions; require documented failover behavior and RTO/RPO for model endpoints.
Reserved planning ask: propose dedicated GPU pool per region (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) with automatic routing + hot standby capacity.
Failover headroom: customer expects 20-30% headroom reserved for cross-region failover. Wants clear pricing and billing model for headroom vs active capacity.
Canary/rollout: request canary that limits to 5% traffic with automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized variant on overload.
POC milestones: baseline latency run -> autoscaling stress test -> cross-region failover drill -> SLA draft review.
Quote from VP Eng: 'We need deterministic latency at scale; if failover costs double, we need a transparent trade-off.'
Security notes: legal insists on KMS key control (customer-managed), audit logs for token-level tracing, and data residency for EU customers.
Pricing negotiations: they prefer committed monthly reserve with defined throughput guarantees and credits for SLA breaches.
Internal ask: SE to produce reserve-sizing matrix (per-region GPU count + expected per-GPU throughput) and failure simulation notes.
Action items: deliver region-by-region capacity table, sample SLA language for 95/99p, and cost delta for 20% vs 30% failover headroom.
Red flags: their procurement wants hard SLAs in contract; finance flagged estimated ARR at upper bound only if SLAs accepted.
